headline: Prior biological knowledge built into transcriptomic deep learning architectures
label: Knowledge Guided Transcriptomic Models
summary: Transcriptomic models increasingly encode gene regulatory priors, LLM gene knowledge, and pathway topology directly in their architectures.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is embedding established biological knowledge directly into model structure so that predictions remain anchored to known biology. scTransformer injects gene regulatory priors into Transformer attention for scRNA-seq and improves cell-type classification. scLLM-DSC fuses NCBI gene-prior LLM embeddings with a graph-guided topological view through cross-modal contrastive alignment for scRNA-seq clustering. PathTIGR combines pathway topology with cancer genomic variants via attention and transformer modules to predict immunotherapy response, and SpaVGMC aligns representations with spatial graphs. Not every item shares this emphasis: TifBERT applies self-supervised masked gene modeling to normalization-robust bulk RNA-seq, and TopoMIL adds sample-level cell-distribution topology to multiple instance learning on microscopy images. What is new is LLM-derived gene knowledge and regulatory scaffolds appearing as built-in components of the model.
